items.title: Canonicalize scope contract paths at write and compare boundaries
items.context: Resolve configured source-root-relative paths such as core/foo.ts to one persisted repo-root-relative packages/main/src/core/foo.ts representation; normalize separators/dot segments, reject absolute/traversal/symlink escapes, preserve exact/subtree semantics, version legacy reads, and ship behind a path-canonicalization rollout flag whose rollback reads prior signed artifacts without rewriting them.
items.userSees: The terminal prints: "input: core/foo.ts | canonical: packages/main/src/core/foo.ts | rule: allowed_modify | status: PASS".

happy.desc: Source-root-relative core/foo.ts and repo-root-relative packages/main/src/core/foo.ts canonicalize to the same persisted repo-root-relative path, and exact-file versus declared-subtree matching keeps its existing semantics.
POSIX dot segments and Windows separators normalize deterministically (for example ./core/../core/foo.ts and core\foo.ts) without changing the canonical repo-root-relative identity.

With path canonicalization enabled, newly written scope artifacts carry the canonical path and schema/version identity, while rollback mode can read a previously signed legacy artifact without rewriting or silently re-signing its history.

edge.desc: Inputs already canonical remain idempotent, source-root and repo-root bases are distinguished explicitly, and an input valid under more than one plausible base is rejected as ambiguous rather than guessed.

A symlink that resolves inside the permitted repository boundary is compared by its canonical repository identity, while path-prefix collisions such as src/core2 versus src/core do not count as subtree matches.

Legacy, missing, or changed path-canonicalizer versions are surfaced as migration/stale or re-attestation outcomes according to policy; the independent path rollout flag does not alter AST-anchor rollout state.

adversarial.desc: Absolute POSIX/Windows paths, drive/UNC paths, traversal above the repository or configured source root, and symlink escapes are rejected fail-closed at both write and compare boundaries.
Crafted separator, case/prefix, dot-segment, encoded traversal, or mismatched-base inputs cannot expand allowedModify/files.modify scope or turn an out-of-scope file into an exact/subtree match.

Failure output identifies original input, attempted canonical form or rejection reason, selected base, canonicalizer version, and matching rule so operators can repair the contract without bypassing it.

items.title: Use parser-backed enclosing declarations for semantic anchors
items.context: Replace regex nearestTsAnchor behavior with versioned AST anchors that prefer functions/methods/classes/interfaces/types/top-level intended declarations, never control flow or local const, preserve protected-anchor fail-closed semantics, and ship behind an independent AST-anchor rollout flag; parser-version drift must require stale/re-attestation and rollback must not reinterpret or rewrite signed history.
items.userSees: The terminal prints: "anchor: function resumeBreakerState | anchorParserVersion: ts-ast-v1 | status: PASS" and never reports "anchor: if" or a local const.

happy.desc: For edits inside a TypeScript function, nested function, class method, or constructor, parser-backed anchoring selects the nearest enclosing intended declaration with stable kind/name identity instead of a textual nearest match.
Class, interface, type, enum, namespace, function, method, and supported top-level declaration edits emit versioned AST anchors that semantic-scope comparison can match deterministically.
Protected declarations remain fail-closed: changing a protected anchor is blocked, while a permitted edit under the same enclosing declaration passes with anchor kind/name/parser-version evidence.

edge.desc: Nested declarations choose the innermost enclosing declaration appropriate to the changed range; edits between declarations use the documented top-level/file fallback rather than borrowing a sibling declaration.

Overloads, anonymous/default-export constructs, computed methods, multiline signatures, decorators, and declaration merging retain deterministic identities; removing or renaming a real declaration remains observable rather than being hidden by continuity heuristics.

AST-anchor rollout and rollback are independent from path canonicalization; parser/schema-version change marks prior anchors stale or requiring re-attestation and rollback reads signed historical anchors without reinterpretation or rewrite.

adversarial.desc: if/else, for/for-of/for-in, while/do, switch, catch/try, and local variable declarations such as const storyId are never emitted as semantic declaration anchors; edits within them bind to the enclosing function/method/class or documented file scope.
Malformed supported TypeScript, unsupported syntax, parse recovery ambiguity, deletion, rename, overload-count loss, and anchor-kind mismatch cannot fail open to an allowed local/control-flow anchor.
Semantic-scope diagnostics expose file, changed range, selected enclosing declaration, anchor kind/name, parser and artifact versions, protected/out-of-scope rule, and stale/re-attestation reason.

items.title: Classify official shared B-META gap metadata safely
items.context: Treat B-META framework-audit findings as shared lifecycle metadata only when mechanically bound to official gap_log provenance/content (signed or digest-bound command event/receipt). Missing, stale, mismatched, forged, direct-edited, arbitrary B-META and unknown .lattice files remain fail-closed; classification must not be path-only.
items.userSees: The terminal prints: "shared metadata: B-META-framework-audit/findings.json | writer: gap_log | contentBinding: valid | status: PASS"; forged input prints "status: BLOCKED".

happy.desc: A B-META framework-audit finding written through official gap_log is classified as trusted shared lifecycle metadata only when its command/process event or receipt provenance is authentic and its digest binds the exact persisted content, path, and relevant story/framework identity.

An unchanged officially bound gap_log finding does not make an unrelated story dirty or block done_prepare, while the classifier reports the trusted registry class and provenance rule that admitted it.

Official updates create a new content/provenance binding atomically; the prior binding cannot be reused for modified content and ordinary story-owned or runtime metadata keeps its existing classification.

edge.desc: Missing receipt/event, stale head/material/content binding, mismatched digest, wrong command, wrong B-META artifact, wrong story/framework identity, or incomplete write is classified as untrusted/blocking with a distinct actionable reason.

Equivalent serialization rules are explicit: only the canonical digest representation is accepted, and timestamp/order/whitespace changes either reproduce the bound digest by specification or require a new official binding rather than path-based trust.
Legacy official gap_log artifacts without the new binding follow an explicit migration/re-attestation path and never become trusted merely because they live under the B-META path.

adversarial.desc: Forged receipts/events/signatures, replayed provenance from another finding, digest collision-shaped inputs, path substitution, and copied valid provenance attached to different content are rejected fail-closed.
Direct edits, arbitrary B-META files, non-framework-audit findings, unknown .lattice paths, symlink/path alias tricks, and files merely named like official metadata remain blocking/untrusted.

Diagnostics reveal classifier class, canonical artifact path, expected versus observed content/provenance digest, event/receipt identity and freshness, and the exact remediation command without leaking or treating prose as proof.

items.title: Prove migration diagnostics and adversarial scope behavior
items.context: Add focused tests for source/repo/Windows/dot/traversal/symlink paths; independent rollout/rollback combinations; legacy/path/parser version staleness; if/for/while/switch/catch/local const/nested functions/methods/classes/top-level anchors; protected/out-of-scope blocking; B-META valid provenance versus missing/stale/mismatch/forged/direct-edit/unknown negatives; and diagnostics exposing original/canonical/anchor/version/rule.
items.userSees: The focused verification ends with: "canonical scope path + AST anchor + provenance migration matrix: PASS" and includes original/canonical/version/rule diagnostics.

happy.desc: Focused smoke coverage exercises source-root, repo-root, Windows-separator, and dot-segment path inputs and proves equivalent paths converge to one canonical identity with exact/subtree behavior preserved.

Focused semantic smoke coverage proves enclosing anchors for functions, nested functions, methods, constructors, classes, interfaces/types and documented top-level scope, including stable overload behavior and protected-anchor blocking.
End-to-end gap_log/closeout coverage proves an officially provenance-bound B-META finding is admitted as shared metadata and done_prepare remains usable for an unrelated story.

The path and AST rollout flags are tested independently in all enabled/disabled combinations, including rollback reading signed legacy/versioned artifacts without mutation and forward re-enable producing current-version artifacts.

edge.desc: Migration tests cover missing/legacy/current/future or changed canonicalizer, anchor parser, and artifact versions, and assert the exact accept, stale, migrate, or re-attest outcome without rewriting signed history.

Anchor matrices cover if/for/while/switch/catch/local const, multiple changes in one declaration, nested ranges, between-declaration changes, overloads, deletion and rename so coverage cannot pass by checking only a simple function fixture.

Diagnostics assertions require original and canonical path/base, declaration kind/name/range, canonicalizer/parser/artifact version, provenance digest/freshness, classifier/match rule, and a concrete remediation for every rejected or stale case.

adversarial.desc: Negative path tests include absolute POSIX, drive and UNC paths, traversal, ambiguous bases, prefix collisions, symlink escapes and separator/dot obfuscation; every case remains fail-closed at write and comparison boundaries.

Negative metadata tests include missing, stale, mismatched, forged, replayed and content-substituted provenance, direct edits, arbitrary B-META, symlink aliases and unknown .lattice files; no case is admitted by path alone.

Process-fact contract verification binds every new gate-consumed version, provenance, classifier and diagnostic semantic, and regression tests prove rollback or legacy compatibility cannot bypass protected/out-of-scope gates.
